_comment: What site_base.py runs, never what it writes by hand. Every project starts from its framework's official create CLI and every package arrives through `pnpm add <name>` with no version: pnpm resolves the newest release that is at least 3 days old (pnpm.minimumReleaseAge, also passed to `pnpm dlx`). No version lives here except a constraint with its reason (`constraints`). A security fix younger than that is let in by security_fix.py, exact release only. `fresh_allow` lists packages the versions gate lets stay behind the newest major, with the reason.

quality_tools._comment: tools/quality: SonarJS and dependency-cruiser need the TypeScript JavaScript API, which TypeScript 7 does not ship, so this folder installs TypeScript 6 (a constraint, not a pin). @babel/parser counts code comments for the per-file ratchet.

cloudflare._comment: Added to the site repo when site.yaml provider is cloudflare. The cf CLI runs through `pnpm dlx cf@latest` under the same 3-day rule.

vercel._comment: Runs through `pnpm dlx vercel@latest` under the 3-day rule when site.yaml provider is vercel.

motion.notes: Added only when the spec asks for motion or 3D: `pnpm add <name>`, no version.

astro.why: Almost no JavaScript on the wire, content in Markdown.
astro.notes: Static output by default; `pnpm astro add <adapter>` only when a page needs a server.

nextjs.why: Server rendering and metadata for pages that must be indexed.
nextjs.notes: Server components by default; the create CLI also writes AGENTS.md, Next's own guide for coding agents. `next typegen` writes the route types (LayoutProps, PageProps) that tsc needs.

tanstack.why: Public pages rendered on the server plus a fast private app.
tanstack.notes: The create CLI wires the provider's adapter (--deployment) and writes wrangler.jsonc for Cloudflare. `tsr generate` writes src/routeTree.gen.ts.

security_tools._comment: Installed with Homebrew, their official installer on macOS and Linux, and kept current by it. Semgrep's registry rules are under the Semgrep Rules License v1.0.

pnpm._comment: Written into pnpm-workspace.yaml of every site. minimumReleaseAge is minutes (3 days): known npm supply-chain attacks were caught and pulled within hours to two days, so a 3-day wait skips them without holding back ordinary updates. trustPolicy blocks a package whose publisher trust dropped; versions older than trustPolicyIgnoreAfter (6 months) are not judged, and trustPolicyExclude names a package measured to trip it with no incident (chromium-bidi, under lighthouse). strictDepBuilds fails on an install script nobody approved (built_dependencies, written as allowBuilds). Overrides force a patched transitive release; drop one when its parent moves past it. A security fix younger than 3 days goes under minimumReleaseAgeExclude through security_fix.py: exact versions only, removed once old enough.

constraints.typescript@6: astro check (astro stack) and SonarJS and dependency-cruiser (tools/quality) say they do not support TypeScript 7 yet; each tool's own message asks for TypeScript 6. Drop the constraint when they do.

fresh_allow.@types/node: its types follow the Node.js major the site runs on, not the newest Node.js
